[budget2026_real_gdp_growth]
economy expanded by 1.5 per cent in 2025. Looking ahead, the economy is forecast to grow by 1.3 per cent in 2026 before increasing to 1.8 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_nominal_gdp_growth]
Nominal GDP growth in 2025 has been revised up to 4.1 per cent from 3.8 per cent, and up to 4.4 per cent from 4.1 per cent in 2026

[budget2026_employment_growth]
employment in B.C. will increase by 0.4 per cent in 2026 (approximately +12,900 jobs), followed by annual growth of 0.8 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_unemployment_rate]
unemployment rate is expected to average 5.9 per cent in 2026 and 5.8 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_population_growth]
population is projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026, relecting net outlows of temporary residents following several years of elevated inlows. Population growth is expected to remain low in 2027, rising by just 0.4 per cent

[budget2026_retail_sales_growth]
Retail sales are forecast to moderate to 2.4 per cent growth in 2026, rise to 3.3 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_cpi_growth]
consumer price inlation is forecast to be 2.1 per cent in 2026, and 2.0 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_housing_starts]
expects B.C. housing starts to total approximately 44,210 units in 2026 and 45,920 units in 2027

[budget2026_exports_growth]
real exports of goods and services are projected to increase by a modest 1.6 per cent, relecting weak global demand and continued trade uncertainty. The Ministry expects real exports of goods and services to grow by 4.2 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_overnight_rate]
overnight target rate will average 2.28 per cent in 2026 and 2.60 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_goc_10y_rate]
10-year Government of Canada bond rate is assumed to be 3.34 per cent in 2026 and 3.49 per cent in 2027

[budget2026_cad_per_usd]
Canadian dollar will average 73.6 US cents in 2026 and 75.6 US cents in 2027
